title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 44: Defense witness scrutinized, flame transition removed
summary: The 43rd day of Vice President Sara Duterte"s impeachment trial saw the House prosecution and defense counsel clash over the capacity of witness AML Consulting PH founder Rainer Dela Fuente to answer…

blocks.text: The 43rd day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial saw the House prosecution and defense counsel clash over the capacity of witness AML Consulting PH founder Rainer Dela Fuente to answer questions.

The beginning of the trial, however, was marked by a strange moment wherein during the prayer of Senator-judge Alan Peter Cayetano, there was a flame transition during the livestream. The moment caught the attention of netizens online, with many finding the mishap comedic.

The trial opened with an unusual moment when a flame transition appeared on the livestream while Senator-judge Alan Peter Cayetano was leading the prayer. The unexpected visual caught the attention of netizens, many of whom found the livestream mishap amusing.

Senate impeachment presiding officer Francis Escudero later ordered the transition edited out of the livestream, with the Senate Public Relations and Information Bureau (PRIB) apologizing for the incident.
Defense counsel Mark Vinluan presented Dela Fuente, a CPA lawyer and former investigator for the Anti-Money Laundering Council.

House prosecutor Chel Diokno objected to Dela Fuente being a witness, pointing out that Duterte was not facing a charge of money laundering. Vinluan argued that there was a portion of the impeachment article stating that there may have been money laundering. =
Escudero said that the defense had leeway in presenting evidence.

Vinluan presented various clips of former president Rodrigo Duterte, the late senator Miriam Defensor-Santiago, and the late Chief Justice Renato Corona, asking Dela Fuente for his opinions on their statements.
Diokno objected to the line of questioning, with several senator-judges raising concerns about presenting video statements from people who could not be questioned.
Vinuluan also quizzed Dela Fuente on portions of financial forensic analyst Alexander Cabrera’s report, which alleged that Duterte had unexplained wealth amounting to P817 million.

The matter of Dela Fuente’s capacity to answer questions became a running question among the prosecution and the senator-judges, especially when it was revealed that Dela Fuente did not even read Cabrera’s report. Neither did he read the impeachment articles nor other evidence presented before the court.

Dela Fuente would later clarify that he was not discounting Cabrera’s report, as he was only asked hypothetical questions. He maintained that he could only compare the portions being presented to him with the law.

On other matters, Escudero allowed the witness from the Center for International Expositions and Missions (CITEM), department manager Rowena Mendoza, to be replaced by CITEM chief of Corporate Planning Eva Marie Mariquina. —LDF, GMA News
